concert.event: Oscar Peterson - Words and Music (BBC TV-series)

CE_note: Coleman Hawkins had been contacted by Director Yannick Bruynuoghe to come from New York to play at the first Adolphe Sax festival in Dinant (birthplace of Sax) – he stayed two days more for the shooting of the film. Arvanitas, Woode and Fields were Hawk's accompanists in Dinant
Baker was added for the films. Arvanitas, Baker and Fields came from Paris

Woode from Sweden. The numbers were chosen by the mutual agreement of Hawkins and Yannick Bruynoghe. Filming took two days (4th & 5th June 1962). So here is a rare opportunity to see and hear the master tenorist Coleman Hawkins in top form. From the initial free style warm-up through mixed tempo blues to the ballad Just One More Chance he never fails to excite. French piano star Georges Arvanitas is an impressive companion, as is legendary virtuoso Earl Hines in the second half, although his vocals may be an acquired taste.
Eddie Cook (Publisher and Editor-in-Chief, Jazz Journal International)

On this evening, which was the final one from the 1972 edition of the Loosdrecht Jazz festival, three groups were present:
- Friends of Jazz [winner of the Loosdrecht Jazz Concours 1972]
- James Moody/Jimmy Owens Quintet
- Charles Mingus Group
The concert by James Moody/Jimmy Owens Quintet also got a radio broadcast by NOS radio.
It seems that the Dutch public broadcaster VARA also presented footage of those three groups on national television on August 16, 1972.

concert.CE_note: Two days after the release of the Head Hunters album

The show was part of Mike Azarin’s concert series called “Twilight Concerts on the Lawn”. Opening up that night was Larry Coryell’s Eleventh House with Alphonse Mouzon on drums before the Headhunters took the stage in front of 4500 people. The rendition of "Palm Grease" seems to be the earliest floating around at the moment - the band had cut the "Thrust" album earlier the same month.

CE_note: Coleman Hawkins had been contacted by Director Yannick Bruynuoghe to come from New York to play at the first Adolphe Sax festival in Dinant (birthplace of Sax) – he stayed two days more for the shooting of the film. Arvanitas, Woode and Fields were Hawk's accompanists in Dinant
Baker was added for the films. Arvanitas, Baker and Fields came from Paris

Woode from Sweden. The numbers were chosen by the mutual agreement of Hawkins and Yannick Bruynoghe. Filming took two days (4th & 5th June 1962). So here is a rare opportunity to see and hear the master tenorist Coleman Hawkins in top form. From the initial free style warm-up through mixed tempo blues to the ballad Just One More Chance he never fails to excite. French piano star Georges Arvanitas is an impressive companion, as is legendary virtuoso Earl Hines in the second half, although his vocals may be an acquired taste.
Eddie Cook (Publisher and Editor-in-Chief, Jazz Journal International)

concert.CE_note: "They played a suite especially written for this occasion. A piece that showed some of the aspects in the music of the multidirectional Anthony Braxton. Wheeler and Braxton matched each other beautifully, Wheeler is a musician who has much in common with Braxton, an intellectual player with a cool sound and a good ear for Braxton's intricate written lines. Their performance ended with a bebop-like tune, and drummer Bobo Shaw (from Black Artists Group from St. Louis, BAG) who throughout the piece had revealed himself as a very musical and inventive drummer, kept the music on fire." - Ib Skovgaard Petersen

concert.CE_note: World Premier 10. December 1999. A coproduction with RTBF - Belgian Radio - Television.

Le 6 février 1965 Chuck Berry se retrouve au studio Universal à Waterloo pour l'enregistrement d'une émission qui sera diffusée, quelques mois plus tard, le 11 mai.Le rocker américain est alors accompagné par des musiciens de jazz belge, le pianiste Willy Albimoor (disparu en 2004), le bassiste Roger Vanhaverbeke (aka Ed Rogers, disparu en 2011), et le guitariste Willy Donni (disparu en 2017).L'enregistrement est réalisé dans le cadre de l'émission "Face au Public" qui se consacrait, à chaque édition, à mettre en avant une grande star de la musique pop/rock ou de la chanson, jouant devant un public.

concert.CE_note: 38 minutes 42 secondes de délire : Zappa joue au début sur She's too much for my mirror. Il présente le groupe en avertissant le public qu'il pourrait manquer quelque chose s'il n'y prenait garde, il arrose l'harmonica de Beefheart pendant que celui-ci joue. Break. Zappa : Captain Bullshit !. Van Vliet : That's a good name. Et ils reprennent. L'orchestre interprète My human gets me blues, Wild Life, Hobo Chang Ba, et les vingt minutes finales de When Big Joan sets up avec Zappa... J'ai déjà raconté comme j'enjambe les barrières et vais interroger F.Z. pendant trois quarts d'heure, ce qui entamera une suite de rencontres dans les années qui suivent, comment le Capitaine me traverse comme un ectoplasme... J'attendrai aussi trente ans pour aller voir Robert Wyatt à Louth pour Jazz Magazine...

concert.CE_title: Art Blakey And His New Jazz Messengers

CE_note:
The first Total Music Meeting took place on November 7-10, 1968 at the Quartier von Quasimodo in Berlin. The TMM, conceived as an alternative to the Berliner Jazztage usually held at the more formal Philharmonie, was organized by the musicians themselves, including Brötzmann, Kowald, Hampel, Alexander von Schlippenbach, and Jost Gebers. Apparently "Peter Brötzmann and his Free Big Band" were booked for the 1968 Jazztage, but Brötzmann refused to comply with the Philharmonie dress code, and he was replaced by Don Cherry's Big Band, which performed Cherry's "Eternal Rhythm" on the evening of November 9.
This is just a fragment of the November 1968 incarnation of the Peter Brötzmann Group. Also booked at this TMM were the Globe Unity Orchestra
Gunter Hampel's Time is Now Group with Hampel (vb, fl), John McLaughlin (g), Arjen Gorter (b), Laurie Allen (d), and Roel Koes (electronics, g), joined by guests Sonny Sharrock and Pharoah Sanders
the Donata Höfer Group with Höfer (p, vln), Jost Gebers (b), and Manfred Kussatz (d)
the Manfred Schoof Quintet with Schoof (tpt, flh), Michel Pilz (bcl), Alexander Von Schlippenbach (p), Buschi Niebergall (b), and John Stevens (d)

and the Spontaneous Music Ensemble with Stevens, Trevor Watts (as, fl), and Maggie and Carol-Ann Nichols (voc). Musicians from one group joined other groups on some performances -- everything must have been quite fluid.

Ses musiciens : Au piano : Marty NAPOLEON, à la clarinette : Joe MURANYI, Danny BARCELONA à la batterie, Tyree GLENN au trombone, et Buddy CATLETT à la basse. 
La chanteuse noire JOEL ASELBROWN (?) chante "Bill Bayley won't you please come home".
Louis ARMSTRONG interprète "Muskrat ramble", "Mack the knife" et "When the saints go marchin'in".

Claude LUTER et ses musiciens interprètent "Les oignons" et "Apex blues".
Louis ARMSTRONG et Tyree GLENN, travesti en femme (allusion à la regrettée chanteuse Velma Middleton, longtemps partenaire d'Armstrong)) chantent en duo, d'une manière humoristique, "That's my desire" 
Ils sont accompagnés de Buddy CATLETT à la basse, Marty NAPOLEON au piano, Joe MURANYI à la clarinette et Danny BARCELONA à la batterie. 
Louis ARMSTRONG, accompagné de son orchestre, joue et chante "Cabaret", "Blueberry hill", "You'll never walk alone" et "When it's sleeypy time down south". 
Il joue un morceau instrumental pur et un morceau instrumental chanté "Ladies et gentlemen as I said before" (2 derniers morceaux non inclus dans le matériel numérisé)

Prestation de Bobby HUTCHERSON au vibraphone. Il est accompagné de Harold LAND au saxo, Joe CHAMBERS à la batterie, Reggie JOHNSON à la basse et Stanley COWELL au piano. 
Début et fin du concert du 26 Juillet 1969 de Miles DAVIS et son Quintet composé de Dave HOLLAND (bassiste), Chick COREA (piano), Wayne SHORTER au saxo et Jack DEJOHNETTE à la batterie. Improvisations autour des thèmes suivants : "Directions" (de 20'52'' à 27' , "Spanish Key" (de 27' à 36'50''), "Fall in Love Too Easily" (de 36'48'' à 40'35'') suivi du début de "Masqualero" (shunté) puis en fin de concert "Nefertiti" (de 42'34'' à 51'34'') puis une dernière impro sur un thème non identifié.

+media.title: Trois styles trois époques [1957-09-12]
+media.CE_tracklist:
- L'orchestre d'Armand GORDON (avec Raymond FONSEQUE) interpréte un classique du style "New Orleans", "Buddy's habit" de King OLIVER puis une composition de Lil HARDIN-ARMSTRONG, "Dropping Shucks".
- L'orchestre de Maxime SAURY avec Jean-Claude NAUDE à la trompette, Michel CAMICAS au trombone, Maurice MARTIN à la batterie, Jacques DENJEAN au piano, Guy REY à la contrebasse interpréte "Them There Eyes" puis "Creole love call" de Duke ELLINGTON et "I've found a new baby".
- "Middle jazz" avec l'orchestre de Claude BOLLING composé de Bernard HULIN à la trompette, Claude GOUSSET au trombone, Gérard BADINI à la clarinette, Pierre GOSSEZ au saxo ténor, Pierre MICHELOT à la contrebasse et Arthur MOTTA à la batterie qui joue successivement "Jive at five" de Harry EDISON puis "Frankie and Johnnie" et en fin le thème du film "Jammin' the blues".
- Un trio composé de Martial SOLAL au piano, Pierre MICHELOT à la contrebasse et Kenny CLARKE à la batterie interpréte un thème intitulé "Love me or leave me".
- Un quintet formé par Martial SOLAL au piano, Pierre MICHELOT à la contrebasse, Kenny CLARKE à la batterie, Sacha DISTEL à la guitare et Bobby JASPAR à la flûte traversière interpréte un thème intitulé "There will never be another you".
- Lucky THOMPSON improvise sur le thème de "I'll remember April" accompagné par Martial SOLAL au piano, Pierre MICHELOT à la contrebasse et Kenny CLARKE.
- Pour le final de l'émission, une formation composée de Martial SOLAL au piano, Pierre MICHELOT à la contrebasse, Kenny CLARKE à la batterie, Sacha DISTEL à la guitare, Bobby JASPAR et Lucky THOMPSON au saxophone joue un blues.

This is part of Chick's nearly 2 month long 75th birthday residency at the Blue Note. A few things seem to be up on youtube from bits and pieces of a few shows, but I think this will be the first complete set from a night.
As you can imagine and will hear, this is really a special pairing that results in a great performance. It was the first of 3 duet nights (Herbie Hancock for night 2, and Gonzalo Rubalcaba for night 3). Chick referred to this night as a Premiere because he and Brad have apparently not played together before this. I'm certainly hoping the experience is repeated and more properly documented. The playing and possibilities with these 2 are phenomenal.Green Dolphin will knock socks off.
I'm hoping more of the nights from this whole run at the Blue Note might pop up from others. It didn't seem that this show was being officially recorded or filmed, as things had been at a Chick's residency when he turned 60. Really hoping to hear the Return to Forever meets Mahavishnu shows that close out this run. In the meantime, we can enjoy this.
Please support these great artists by purchasing their officially released material and by paying to see them live.

comments:
another from the concerts, tours and bands not heard in etree dept. In the extremely busy and active career of Chick Corea, this was one of the last bands he played in (Maybe even the last) before he found and stuck with an obscure little band called Return to Forever. Actually, Corea hasn't played in many obscure bands at all, this May be his most obscure of all, since it was only together for one tour, and not a very long one. I think this is also Chick's first band where he was bandleader, since a year earlier he was keyboard player/sideman for the God of Jazz himself, Miles Davis. This is probably the most avant-garde Corea I've ever heard, and the Miles influence is rather hefty even without a trumpet in this group. This couldn't be more different music than the carefully structured music of RTF. It's also to help celebrate one of the greatest 40 year careers anyone's ever had. If Chick Corea isn't in the jazz hall of fame, they need to rebuild it. He is clearly right up there with Miles and Coltrane as a musical pioneer and legendary concert performer, selling out concerts in 1969 and 2008 and not doing it with very much cheese jazz. Chick does play some of that, but not in here or any of my many Chick posts. He does like to use alot of
synthesizer with RTF, but not here, this is piano Chick, much like my 1972 RTF post. Nothing with Anthony Braxton in it sounds like RTF, including this show.

comments:
I did not see this concert, and neither did the source of this recording for me, but it is a good clean recording and seems to be complete (as in uncut), as well as the only 1977 Ponty show I have that qualifies as a full length Ponty set of this time, a very good time for Ponty. (the others
were as an opening act, except Boston 10/77 which was a 2-show night.) This also has some songs not heard in any of those others and it's a very fine show. New orleans is supposed to be a really good place to hear music of many kinds, and any place is a good place to hear a Ponty show from this era. If you haven't heard this one yet, you should. Although he didn't see/record this either, this one comes from the Doctor (of Stud Muffin Productions fame) and anything that he gave me was always good sound quality. The violin solo is extra long in this show and you get a hefty sampling of music from Enigmatic Ocean (the 4th release of Ponty with his own bands). My favorite Ponty band is the
one before this but this is also a very (arm)strong band. Ralph is very good here (as usual for him) and does a nice jam in struggle of the turtle. This was just a few months before Daryl Steurmer joined up with Genesis, and this tour May have had something to do with why Genesis would ask him to try filling Steve Hackett's shoes (a very tall order for anyone). How many know Daryl is the 1st American (he's from Milwaukee, I'm told) to play in Genesis, who is as British as, well, Queen
Elizabeth II, and almost equally royally British. Daryl is a very good guitarist too, and this was when that was becoming clear. He was already very good before ever joining Genesis, and that didn't
hurt either. If you like Daryl for his guitar in Genesis you might like this even more because the guitar has to be strong in a Ponty show, just like the whole band. It's not all about Ponty at a Ponty concert, but if you like his playing, you'll like this playing. One of the reasons Hackett left Genesis is because the guitar was getting too subdued. I like Daryl in Genesis too (espec. 78-81 era) but this was some of the best playing I've ever heard from him (also UConn and Lenox 77) which is part of why there's only one or less of other Ponty tours coming or up from me, and 3 from 77. If I had more from earlier I would share it. The 75-78 Ponty stuff is very good live. I split my copy of this starting disc 2 with track 7 (there are a couple of quiet seconds opening it) which is about halfway
through the show, but there are a couple of other places equally suitable if preferred.

+media.CE_tx:lineage: This is my personal thank you for all the great shows I received from this site. Also, an invitation for some of you to post something really rare this week. We all need to hear this. This is Trane s holy grail missing Newport show from 1961. I recently located my master cassette that I transferred from a reel to reel master mono soundboard back in the late 70 s. I figured that I would give my Nakamichi a try on this recording and go straight into my Phillips CRD with no EQ or messing. This recording has such an intimate feel, you can hear Trane tap in the count for Impressions and you can image the sitting on the wood floor on stage listening to this show. You can hear the squeak of Elvin s hi hat during Naima. Remember this is a recording from 1961. Trane used two bassists on this show, Art Davis and Reggie Workman and hadn't settle on Jimmy Garrison yet but McCoy and Elvin are here. The announcer introduces the first song as So What but Trane rips into Impressions instead. I ve never traded this show but it s time for everyone to hear it. It s a shame there isn t more.

comments:
this is the only recording I've heard yet from the inner worlds
era, the last Maha. Orch. album and tour. there were not alot of shows on this tour since Shakti was already under way in mid 75. the quality varies some, mainly because the bass is too loud in parts (and Ralph Armstrong has a loud, strong style of playing) but it comes from a master made with a Sony TC56 cassette deck and unknown model Sony tieclip mike. this is a raw transfer, only level balancing and some individual loud clap reduction was done, no EQ or noise reduction or other processing was applied. this recording has likely seen some tape circulation, but this is the 1st time I know of it being posted. some might find it a bit annoying that there's all of 1 song in this show from Inner Worlds. Others May be glad, since all the rest is from the original lineup repertoire. If you're wondering how many McLaughlin on guitar/synth shows there are, probably more than this, the only one I've heard.
he mentions having a new instrument, a guitar synthesizer before playing All in the Family. I think the tape flip was before Sanctuary, not sure, but there is just one tape flip (rec. on a 90 min. cassette) there was one of these shows at Brandeis Univ. in Waltham, Mass. around this same time but I've yet to hear a recording of it, or even hear of there being a recording of it. if anyone has it, please post it up. the sound in there would probably not be very good, and not great here either but it's quite listenable sound quality and these Inner Worlds shows are rather hard to come by. John's experiment with the syntar was not a long one. this was a good show too, lots of fire from a hot band. I don't know how many shows they did after this, but it wasn't many.

+media.CE_tx:lineage:
comments:
I got this in a snail trade many years ago from a fellow in Ohio. The recording is pretty good, the mix is a little off in parts, a little distorted in parts, pretty clear in most parts. (Alot of these RTF college gigs have strange mixing, see my Worcester 2/1/74 show for more evidence of that) White and Corea come through clearly throughout, Clarke and DiMeola's mix varies a little more. Track 7 is about 48 minutes long. This is one of the longer RTF shows
I've heard with Al DiMeola. It is a very good performance. Vulcan Worlds is 22 minutes +. The only tape flip interruption comes just after the acoustic jam, just before theme to the mothership starts the first group segment. You May not even notice the splice. Beyond the 7th galaxy is only about 3 min. (this is not very
unusual) all the other songs are much longer. It sounds like this recording comes from an all normal bias/eq setting tape lineage. (this does tend to help preserve the clarity of a normal-bias/EQ recording, which all analog tapes were until high bias tape came out circa later 70's, whereas an all high-bias tape lineage helps to
keep tape noise down and bass response good.)

+media.CE_tx:lineage:
La Bussola was a famous venue in Versilia, a region just above the city of Viareggio, where lots of Italian and international stars performed over the years. Since Viareggio was the most popular town of the area, the venue was generally associated with it in spite being few kms north.
The famous concerts of La Bussola later moved few km south in a new venue called Bussoladomani (in Lido di Camaiore) where Miles Davis performed in 1990. Here is the 1st volume of a series of jazz shows that were broadcast by RAI tv.
Enjoy!

As indicated in the accompanying details, this is the full source for the bootleg Naked City CD: CD 007 â€” Warne Marsh Live In Las Vegas, 1962. The CD release was of a higher generation and contained numerous drop outs and other flaws including the omission of tracks 7,8,9,10 and 12 so this should be considered an upgrade. +media.CE_notes: JEMS is proud to be able to partner with and present some of the choice recordings in the D & D archives. Some of these recordings have been around for years but none of the master tapes or safety copies in some cases have ever been digitized until now. Dave and Donn taped many shows in and around the Seattle area in the 70's and also were contemporaries of some of the JEMS members. Volume 21 captures jazz guitar great Larry Coryell with his Foreplay band from a KOL FM broadcast recorded by Dave's brother when it was broadcast originally. This is one blistering set of jazz fusion played with the furiosity of Mahavishnu Orchestra but with a looseness and swing of rock along the lines of Little Richard that was usually missing in most jazz fusion stews of this time.

+media.CE_notes:
This is a Second Generation copy of a Reel to Reel Soundboard recorded
with microphones placed at the stage amps. The equipment is unknown. This is NOT from the TV Broadcast or from a soundboard that the band may possess. It is an independant soundboard.
In early 1977, I was contacted by a Southern California tape
trader who answered one of my AD's in Trouser Press magazine.
That person did not have anything to trade except the Cal Jam
show from 1974 (which I attended). He had taped all the bands
on a Reel to Reel recorder and separate michrophones he had set
up on the stage. He must have had a small mixer as well as the
recordings picked up all that was played. There is no audience
noise except when the band asked the crowd to make noise (which
was very muted). The only band not recorded was ELP because he
loaded the reel to reel tape upside down and nothing was recorded.
He sent me the remaining bands on TDK-SA cassette tapes. I still
have his copies of Black Sabbath and Deep Purple on those TDK-SA
tapes but due to posting restrictions on this site, they cannot be
shared here. I did send copies to Allan of the CAL JAM web site
and he noted that they sounded better than the official releases!
Unfortunatly, The recordings of Seals & Croft, Black Oak Arkansas
& The Eagles were probably used for blank tapes as these band were
not important to me at the time (Alan could shoot me for that).
The recording of Rare Earth and Earth, Wind and Fire were transfered
to a TDK-D cassette as I needed the SA tape for other recordings.
In spite of that, they still sound great.

+media.CE_notes:
Ricola Notes:
Another broken Reel to Reel tape which I repaired and just finished to transfer on CD.
Editing Notes:
-Original audio had a significant phase error with the left channel leading the right by on average 17 samples, with some variation
-Automatic phase corrections to handle the variations
-Levels started off reasonably balanced, but the right channel became significantly weaker as the recording progressed
-Constant amplification of 3 dB to the left channel, and automatic, varying level adjustments to the right channel to balance with the left
-Original audio was running considerably slow - almost a whole tone, 11.5%, but at least it was consistently off
-Because it was running so slow, the more appropriate new sampling frequency is actually 48 kHz instead of 44.1 kHz in order to preserve more of the information that Ricola captured in the original transfer (not that there's actually very useful detail in those high frequencies here - it's just tape hiss > 10 kHz)
-So instead of resampling (speed adjusting) by 11.5% to correspond to a 44.1 kHz sampling frequency, the resampling factor was only 1.115*44.1/48 = 1.0244 or 2.44%
-All edits done in MATLAB
-ledwhofloyd (Ross), Jan. 2023

Video source: 16 mm master (unknown method of transfer)
Stereo audio source (Ricola): FM Broadcast (Cassette)>trade>wav>Flac

+media.CE_notes:
-the video source comes to me via sewolawen73. It is not a perfect transfer and has some anomalies, but is a significant upgrade to the previously circulating video.
-The picture starts off in color, then there are some weird color "effects" at about 8 in, then it becomes black/white with some intermittent random black minutes speckles, and then finally at about 18 minutes in it becomes color again.
-The mono audio track originally associated with this video source is poor quality.
-Ricola originally seeded the stereo audio source on July 5, 2012, which sounds great. He called it FM, but I suspect it is pre-FM or soundboard because the frequency detail is > 15 kHz.
-The stereo audio has about 30 extra minutes at the end not on the video
-In 2012, matthughen synced Ricola's FM to the previously circulating video version. This is an upgrade to that because I am using a better video quality source. Who knows, maybe an even better source will surface down the line.
-to sync Ricola's stereo audio to this new video source, I first upsampled it to 48 kHz with foobar2000 to match the original mono track and imported it into Audacity.
-the stereo audio doesn't start until about 1:04 into the video, then the FM cuts out again at about 1:34, and then comes back at about 2:40. The band is just getting ready to play during this section so these cuts are disguised on Ricola's audio. I figured out which parts went where.
-the stereo audio was cut with a few seconds of repeated audio (I forget exactly where but I think about 20 minutes in) that I seamlessly removed - the speed adjustment changed from roughly 1% slow before the cut to closer to 0% after
-the stereo audio misses 34:43-35:03 so I had to use the original mono for it
-I used short crossfades for the parts where I joined the original mono with the stereo audio
-I used sync points every 1-2 minutes which keeps a very close match because the speed only drifted by a total of about 0.3% or so on the stereo source within the tape cuts.
-I did some level adjustments to the original mono audio source, and left the stereo audio unchanged except for the resampling to sync it up, and the crossfading
-I kept the original mono audio source for posterity

+media.CE_notes:
Combined from 3 sources to give one continuous version using the best sources for each track.
Repairs have been done to remove clicks, this was the major part of the edit.
Also a little EQ and Normalization was done to even out the sources.
1. Directions * Click removal.
2. Honky Tonk * A 12 second section repeated from 2.08 in the source track has been removed Click removal.
3. What I Say? * Click removal.
4. Sanctuary * Normalized to boost the levels slightly. Click removal.
5. It's About That Time +
6. Yesternow + * # Some Normalization. Cross fades between all three sources were used to complete this track. EQ to source 3.
7. Funky Tonk # Channel patches. EQ
8. Sanctuary # Channel patches. EQ
+Source 1, with male announcer. There were no digital errors noticeable in this source. It sounds as though it has been copied from a vinyl bootleg. Some scratches/clicks were removed. Unfortunately more of 'Yesternow' was not used from this, as there was a scratch/repeated click, which I was unable to remove, so source 3 was used from
# Source 2. This sounds as though it was from a tape source. There were drop-outs in one of the channels. These have been copied from the other channel, and a very little reverb added to maintain the stereo feel. EQ has been added to all of this source, to brighten the top end, and remove a little of the bass, which was booming. The sound is the least clear of the sources
* Source 3, with the female announcer. There were numerous clicks in this source, which appear to come from either a bad disk write, or bad disc rip. Tiny pieces of data were repeated and a jump where the wave form joined itself back together, which looks rather like the disc and data stream were not in synch. The jumps make sharp clicks in the sound.
At least 3 passes were made to remove the clicks. Pass 1 found around 7 (loud) clicks per minute, pass 2 about the same for smaller clicks, pass 3 found around half that number. There are still some clicks I was unable to isolate as they were too deeply embedded in the sound, or could not be isolated from the instruments.
There are some small clicks I have just missed, but I had to call an end to it at some point. These are not particularly noticeable compared with the first pass.
There are sections where the treble becomes muffled, possibly the original tape head picking up dirt, or tape ware. These sections have had a little EQ added to brighten the top end. There are also some cross fades between EQ'ed and raw sections, to cover where hiss cuts in or out in a distracting manner. Some hiss has been left as it was, so that the music is not affected adversely.
After track 4, the recording becomes muffled, particularly in 'It's About that Time', so this source was not preferred from that point onwards.
Were it possible to find the original source for this recording, and make fresh transfer it would provide an improved version.
Final edit. All the sources had tiny gaps between the tracks, these have been removed, and the tracks re-marked.

+media.CE_notes: This is a remaster of the Miles-Trees Miles in Belgium Tree disc #2. Most importantly, I removed the bad clipping throughout Directions (I had to resort to a PC with Adobe Audition for this purpose, nothing capable of doing this on my Mac so far). The second source (starting after the beginning of Keith Jarrett's initial solo in Honky Tonk needed some pitch correction, and I also filtered the modulation noise that accompanied most of the electric piano sound. For the rest, I repaired some minor flaws (I did this a while ago and don't remember all details) and probably applied a small amount of NR and EQ throughout. I also retracked all titles. Due to the pitch correction, the performance no longer fits on one CD. This still remains only B quality but - in my opinion - sounds much nicer than the Miles in B original. Enjoy! And the most important thing: if you have a better version, please share it!

Miles Davis 1971-11-12 Sartory Cologne Germany (remaster) WDR-FM:
Here's the link for the Miles Davis show that Cosmo Lecat posted a few days ago. He merged a couple of sources, but there was a repeated track he didn't notice, besides some other minor problems.
I removed the repeated track, edited the transitions, and mastered everything. The sound was heavily clipped

I restored what I could, filtered out just a little bit of the distortion, made a new tracking, adjusted phase, normalized everything, etc. Anyway, there's still a lot of annoying distortion in the whole set, which is a pity.
The final result has 61 minutes, a couple of minutes more than the original set. I don't know if that's due to different editing or if some version was speed-corrected. Anyway, the musical content is the same.
It sounds a bit better now.

+media.CE_notes: Their first show in Toronto. And believe me, legendary isn’t overstating it. This is one of those shows you make your friends feel shitty about not going to. Former Real Frequency member Samantha captured 53 minutes of Baatin, T3 and Jay Dee (aka J-Dahmer!) on a handheld recorder standing by the stage. So in the tradition of the Real Freqs, it’s raw. But that’s definitely part of its charm. And the quality ain’t actually bad. But how did Slum Village end up in Toronto over a year prior to their first official release, Fantastic Volume 2? How did the Comfort Zone end up packed full of people singing the words to songs that weren’t even out? Who the hell were these guys?Their first effort, a cassette entitled “Fantastic Vol. 1″ crossed the border into Toronto with Moss (yes, the producer behind Ghostface’s “Kilos”) almost 2 years before. I can’t remember if he was returning from school or if he and Mr. Attic (Da Grassroots) had just gone down to Detroit to shop for records. We were already fans of Jay Dee through the work he’d done for Tribe and Pharcyde. We were already anticipating music from the guy. So pretty much it was a no-brainer for Moss and Pee to pick that up when they saw it in the store. They ran that shit all the way back to Toronto and that was that. Moss and Attic are notorious for holding back heat. But once that tape got into my hands it was over.Of course I brought it to the show. And I gave that shit to everyone. And they gave it to everyone. At the time I was still going to York and I can even remember a younger DJ P-Plus asking for a dub. Of course, there was no Serato. Most people had third generation dubs, better known as a “dub of a dub”. Dudes would have layers of hiss on their copies. Of course they had hiss. Moss got the original. I got my dub from him. Dudes would actually come to me cause they knew I had the first generation dub. They had no hope of dubbing the original because Moss isn’t really into hanging with human beings. The fucking tape era baby!!Anyhow, thanks to that tape and a couple of others (Jake One, whaddup!!!), Slum formed a following in T.O. before a lot of other places. Even though people were using the internet, it wasn’t as widespread. And that’s part of what makes this show so special. There are moments in the show where Slum themselves are in disbelief at the crowd’s familiarity with their catalogue. It’s definitely in my top 5 concerts of all time. Da Grassroots opened up and I even got to be a part of the show, which is something I’ll never forget. And for everyone else there, this was the first night they heard actually heard Slum Village.Without tape hiss.Special thanks to Musiklee Inzane for not being at the show. Without you, there wouldn’t have been anyone to record it for.-Arcee

A great time, I was sitting in the front row, next to my old friend Chaka Khan, who I had introduced to a Dutch audience in Holland earlier... and I urged her to get up and sing... the rest is history. Still one of the best funkiest concerts I ever saw.
The band only lacked Paul Schaeffer, for it to be the late show band. Paul I saw later as a bandleader for a musical on Broadway, the Ellie Greenwich Story, with my other friend Annie Golden of The Shirts.

The original LP was not that great sounding. I haven't got the CD source to compare it to, so no notion of whether it was better. Given it's an audience tape, from a LP, from 1971, it's not actually that bad now!

notes: Another of my "shoebox" series, maybe an upgrade over previous shares, your mileage may vary. This is a straight transfer of my XLII tape (1991 vintage cassette with the big Maxell clear window). Seems very close to correct pitch, and a nice mix which is true on all of the tapes I've heard from this show. I like this source, but I'm biased probably, one I've had a very long time and know well. I also have a known lineage 3rd gen on XLII-S that really doesn't sound a nice as this one does.
As on all copies I've ever heard, this tapes cuts in rather roughly during Non Brewed Condiment, cuts and fades during Pud Wud, and resumes during Devil Take The Hindmost, probably due to a tape flip that wasn't caught in time at the mixing desk.
I'm working on getting two of my decks repaired, a NAD 6340 and a Teac A-420, so I may revisit this again sometime. Nothing wrong with my Technics RS-BR465 except high miles. I gave it a good cleaning recently before I started sharing some tapes again here recently.

+media.CE_notes:
Excellent concert. We were so close to the musicians that I was a bit afraid about sticking out my mics holder, which sometimes resulted in occasional minor cracks when I hit one of the mics inadvertently.
But, all in all, I'm really happy I managed to tape the show. It was the first concert this evening and I was slightly late with starting my recording gear, which resulted in about a minute and a half of initial not quite nice cracks and clips but after that the sound remains more stable and quite nice as for the Barbican Centre (I haven't got the best opinion of the acoustics there). I have decided to keep the beginning as it is (yet, it's not too bad) instead of just cutting it off for the sake of preserving the completeness of the concert!
I am not quite sure about the titles as I haven't had enough time to listen to the whole recording yet! Any help will be appreciated!
I've already seeded the concert that followed Robert Glasper Trio, that is Terence Blanchard Quintet but I've done some additional work on that one and will probably reseed next week.

title.id: 10ème festival international de jazz à antibes 1969 : compilation n°1 [1969-07-25]
title.title: 10ème Festival international de jazz à Antibes 1969 : Compilation n°1
title.CE_synopsis: 10ème Festival international de Jazz à Antibes Juan-les-Pins dans la pinède en juillet 1969 : concerts de la formation de François GUIN, celle du vibraphoniste Bobby HUTCHERSON et le quintet de Miles DAVIS enregistré lors de la soirée du 25 Juillet 1969. Présentation d'André FRANCIS.
title.CE_tracklist:
La formation du tromboniste François GUIN, comprenant Gérard BADINI au saxophone tenor, Xavier CHAMBON à la trompette, Teddy MARTIN à la batterie, Ricardo GALEAZZI à la contrebasse et Gérard GAMBUS au piano interprète "Blues for us" de François Guin, "Haïtian fight song" de Charlie Mingus.
Bobby HUTCHERSON, au vibraphone, et Harold LAND au saxo, interprètent "Spiral", un extrait de la musique du film "Blow up" d'Antonioni, composée par Herbie Hancock et "Herzog" .
Ils sont accompagnés de Joe CHAMBERS à la batterie, Reggie JOHNSON à la basse et Stanley COWELL au piano. 
Concert de plus d'une heure du quartet de Miles DAVIS. Avec le contrebassiste Dave HOLLAND, Chick COREA au piano, Wayne SHORTER au saxophone ténor et Jack DEJOHNETTE à la batterie, Miles DAVIS joue successivement "Directions", "Miles runs the Voodoo down", "Milestones", "Footprints", "'Round midnight", "It's about that time" et "Sanctuary".

title.CE_tracklist:
les JAZZ'O MANIACS, un orchestre français, interprète "Miss Anna" et "Immigration blues". Les musiciens sont pieds nus et portent des bermudas fleuris. 
Graham COLLIER Sextet interprète un thème (titre non identifié). Aux côtés de Graham COLLIER à la contrebasse : John MARSHALL à la batterie, Stan SULZMANN au saxo, Nick EVANS au trombone, Harry BECKETT à la trompette et Stanley COWELL au piano.

title.CE_synopsis: 10ème festival international d' Antibes Juan les Pins de Juillet 1969 dans la pinède de Juan avec LES SWINGERS (France), Bobby HUTCHERSON, le vibraphoniste et le quintet de Miles DAVIS avec Dave HOLLAND, Chick COREA, Wayne SHORTER et Jack DEJOHNETTE.
title.CE_tracklist:
L'ensemble les SWINGERS interprète un long thème de jazz style Dixieland "The sandman". Les musiciens : Gérard BADINI au saxo, Xavier CHAMBON à la trompette, François GUIN au trombone, Ricardo GALLEAZZI à la contrebasse, Gérard GAMBUS au piano et Teddy MARTIN à la batterie. 
Prestation de Bobby HUTCHERSON au vibraphone. Il est accompagné de Harold LAND au saxo, Joe CHAMBERS à la batterie, Reggie JOHNSON à la basse et Stanley COWELL au piano. 
Début et fin du concert du 26 Juillet 1969 de Miles DAVIS et son Quintet composé de Dave HOLLAND (bassiste), Chick COREA (piano), Wayne SHORTER au saxo et Jack DEJOHNETTE à la batterie. Improvisations autour des thèmes suivants : "Directions" (de 20'52'' à 27' , "Spanish Key" (de 27' à 36'50''), "Fall in Love Too Easily" (de 36'48'' à 40'35'') suivi du début de "Masqualero" (shunté) puis en fin de concert "Nefertiti" (de 42'34'' à 51'34'') puis une dernière impro sur un thème non identifié.

L'australien PHILIPPE DEUST et son adversaire FRANCOIS JAUFFRET - différentes phases du match - le français est gagnant.

dans cette émission elle chante huit prestations accompagnée de l'orchestre de Tito PUENTE, dont une accompagnée plus spécialement par son mari, Pedro KNIGHT. Quant à Tito PUENTE il accompagne l'orchestre avec diverses percussions et joue incidemment du vibraphone.

Présentation par André FRANCIS.

Ils sont accompagnés de Buddy CATLETT à la basse, Marty NAPOLEON au piano, Joe MURANYI à la clarinette et Danny BARCELONA à la batterie.

Abdullah Ibrahim formerly Dollar Brand, pianist, composer, arranger, was bom in Cape Town, South Africa, in 1934. When Duke Ellington heard him in 1965 he was so impressed that he arranged for Ibrahim to move to
America where he quickly became a leading figure in the jazz avant-garde.

title.title: Arena | The Apollo Story (1)
title.CE_announcement:
he list of artists who have performed at Harlem's Apollo Theater reads like a Who's Who of black American entertainment. No black performer, from Sammy
Davis Jr to Charlie Parker, could be considered a star without conquering the Apollo's tough, sophisticated audience.
Tonight and next week Arena celebrates the 50th anniversary of the Apollo.
But it is more than the story of a single venue. It is the story of Harlem itself and the struggles and triumphs of - black America.
Tonight's programme begins with the Apollo's infancy, when Bill (Bojangles)
Robinson tapped effortlessly to the music of Fats Waller, and royalty like Count Basie and Duke Ellington held court. Honi Coles and the Copasetics, and former chorus girls the Swinging Seniors, re-create the famous dance routines, and Lionel Hampton recalls when the audience went so wild, the upper balcony cracked.
After the war, bebop changed the face of jazz. The anarchy of the Dizzy Gillespie Band mirrored the social changes taking place outside the Apollo's doors, and the theatre shook, rattled and rolled to the R&B pioneers like Louis Jordan and Joe Turner.

title.title: Bath Festival - American Visitors
title.CE_announcement:
The final televised concert from the Bath International Festival, which this year celebrates the performing arts of America.
From Green Park Station,
Bath Lester Bowie 's Brass Fantasy
From Chicago, trumpeter Lester Bowie leads this virtuoso choir of brass soloists, with percussion, in a programme of inventive arrangements of jazz standards, pop songs and original pieces.
The idea for the Brass
Fantasy goes back 15 years.
Lester says, 'I had an idea for an all-brass group with no saxophones and no keyboards. You see the brass players were overshadowed by the saxophonists for a while in jazz. I wanted to do something to show things you would not normally associate with a trumpet.' Introduced by Michael Berkeley

title.title: Bouton Rouge
CE_synopsis:
Pierre Lattès présente ce numéro spécial sur le blues et l'Angleterre. Au sommaire :
 - -- JOHN MAYALL'S BLUESBREAKERS, filmé dans un club de blues, en public, près de Londres. Il est accompagné à la guitare par Mick Taylor (futur guitariste des Rolling Stones).
 - -- TELEGRAMMES : animation pour présenter des infos musicales.
 - -- LES QUICK AU SPEAK EASY.
 - -- LA NUIT DE LA SEMAINE : En semaine, ce jeune homme travaille comme mécanographe, quand arrive le samedi soir, il prend le train pour Paris et passe la soirée au Bus Palladium. La caméra le suit depuis la gare jusqu'à la discothèque puis dans un café et dans le train de banlieue du retour. Sa silhouette cape et cheveux longs ne laisse pas indifférent et attire les commentaires des passants ou du contrôleur de la SNCF. Le videur et la caissière de la discothèque ont eux, une opinion plus favorable de cette jeunesse. Plans de jeunes au café, dans la boite de nuit dansant, écoutant la musique...
 - -- DISQUE ROUGE : Les MOODY BLUES chantent "Nights of white satin" (Séquence de Pierre LATTES

première diffusion dans Bouton rouge du 09/12/1967) 
 - -- PLATEAU : Pierre Lattès reçoit BRIAN AUGER, les TRINITY et JULIE DRISCOLL.
title.CE_tracklist:
- -- JOHN MAYALL chante "Help me baby" (célèbre blues) 
 - -- LES QUICK, au Speak Easy, chantent du rythm' and blues à l'anglaise "Stand by me".
 - -- DIQUE ROUGE : Au Speak Easy, les MOODY BLUES chantent "Nights in white satin" (ATTENTION : le sigle "disque rouge" apparait plusieurs fois à l'écran).

title.title: Bouton Rouge
title.CE_synopsis:
Pierre Lattès présente les différentes séquences de l'émission dont certaines ont été tournées à Cannes, à l'occasion du Midem :
- -- COEUR DE BOEUF SUR LE SABLE avec CAPTAIN BEEFHEART.
- -- PLATEAU avec les SPARKS (groupe de Rythm'n blues, originaire du Mans).
- -- WEEK-END A BOURG : Un dimanche de janvier à Bourg-en-Bresse : des scènes qui respirent l'ennui, un défilé dans les rues, la sortie de la messe, , une cité HLM, un match de rugby et puis dans une salle des fêtes, un orchestre amateur les BLACK POOLS. Ils sont six, peintre, mécano ou employé de bureau et nous expliquent pourquoi ils ont créé cet ensemble, malgré les critiques. Dans le dancing, des couples valsent, des jeunes flirtent ou jouent au flipper. Deux étudiants en technique avouent leur ennui, leurs difficultés à faire les choses qu'ils aiment, à rencontrer les filles... Ils voudraient partir dans une ville moins bourgeoise, s'amuser comme le font les jeunes de la Capitale. Ils sont blessés quand on les traite de "paysans".
- -- DISQUE ROUGE avec les TURTLES et les FAMILY.
- -- Bande annonce du feuilleton "Johnny Hallyday parle".
- -- LES BALLADES DE PENNY avec PENNY NICHOLS, chanteuse folk.
title.CE_tracklist:
- -- CAPTAIN BEEFHEART and His Magic Band, orchestre d'avant-garde de Los Angeles, avec à la guitare RY COODER (futur compositeur de la musique du film "Paris-texas"), chantent, sur la plage de Cannes, "Electricity" et "Shown up and yes I do".
- -- PLATEAU : Les SPARKS chantent "Mojaw mama", "Funky Frankie Broadway" et en fin d'émission "Red dot" (morceau composé pour "Bouton Rouge" et "Day tripper" (en hommage à Otis redding).
- -- DISQUE ROUGE : Les TURTLES chantent un extrait de "She's my girl" (film de promotion) et les FAMILY chantent au Speak Easy "My friend" (ATTENTION : le sigle "Disque Rouge" apparait de temps en temps sur l'écran).
- -- PENNY NICHOLS, filmée dans le salon d'un hôtel de Cannes, chante, en s'accompagnant à la guitare, "Summer rain".

title.title: Buddy Bolden's Children
title.CE_announcement:
A recording session in search of the Bolden sound.
Humphrey Lyttelton and a hand-picked group of musicians made a record last summer in which they tried to reproduce the sound of the Buddy Bolden band. Bolden has been called the first jazz man but his band, which was active at the turn of the century in New Orleans, was never recorded.
Film cameras followed the rehearsal and the recording session in a small studio in south-east London as Humphrey Lyttelton coaxed his men to forget their own ways of playing and adopt the Bolden style.
Taking part are Russell Davies and Pete Strange (trombones) Alan Elsdon (cornet) John Barnes and Randy Colville (clarinets) Jim Bray (bass) Colin Bowden (drums) Keith Graville (guitar) Henry Lowther (violin) and Ron Weatherburn (piano)
(The Coltrane Legacy tomorrow at 7.30pm)

title.title: Cent ans de jazz | Harlem : l'âge d'or
title.CE_synopsis: Deuxième épisode de "Cent ans de jazz" consacré à l'âge d'or de Harlem dans les années 30, à l'époque des grands orchestres et des grands solistes, du Cotton Club, du Savoy et autre Plantation.Des interviews de Eddie JEFFERSON,danseur de claquette, Cab CALLOWAY,Bud FREEMAN, Nat HENTOFF, écrivain au "Village Voice", Leonard FEATHER, écrivain, Cadillac Bob CHERRY, propriétaire d'un club de jazz,Stéphane GRAPELLI alternent avec de nombreux documents d'archives (Library of Congress, INA) : Bill ROBINSON, Jimmy LUNGEFORD et son orchestre, Ethel WATER,Fats WALLER, Billie HOLIDAY, Duke ELLINGTON, Lester YOUNG, Lionel HAMPTON, George GERSHWIN, Teddy WILSON, Lena HORNE, Count BASIE, Coleman HAWKINS, Nat King COLE, Art TATUM, Django REINHARDT et le quintette du Hot Club de France, Benny GOODMAN, Woody JERMAN, Glen MILLER et son orchestre, Ruth BROWN, Arthur Big Boy CRUDUP et Jonas et George CRUDUP.

title.title: Cent ans de jazz | Racines
CE_synopsis: On commence par deux approches du jazz, qui toutes deux en évoquent les racines : une scène à l'église, avec des fidèles noirs qui écoutent un pasteur prêcher et entrent en transe : le jazz est né en partie des gospel songs d'église

d'autre part, dans un pénitencier du Sud, des prisonniers noirs chantent en choeur en battant des céréales en cadence : ils expliquent le pourquoi et le comment de ce genre de rééducation par la musique, qui rappelle inévitablement les chants des travailleurs noirs du coton, autre source du jazz

les deux autres "racines" ne sont pas évoquées : les rythmes africains d'une part, les "songs" folkloriques Irlandais et musiques militaires et airs d'harmonie européens, d'autre part. 
Le blues est à l'honneur : le chanteur de blues Mance LIPSCOMB chante "C C Rider" et un rhythm and blues. Un autre chanteur de blues, Sonny TERRY, évoque son enfance : élevé par son père et "100 femmes différentes"

explique la signification du blues : "c'est quand une femme vous quitte"...Il chante un blues : "Chain and lock on the door", avec panos sur le décor de la pièce. 
A La Nouvelle Orléans : évocation de l'aspect "fédérateur" des musiques des années 1910-1920, qui n'étaient pas encore véritablement du jazz
c'était souvent du "rag". Le pianiste Roosevelt SYKES évoque le quartier de Bourbon street à l'époque
SYKES joue un boogie-woogie en chantant. Evocation des bordels de la N. O. Evocation du légendaire pianiste Jelly Roll Morton

les pianistes de l'époque ? des proxénètes. Evocation du pianiste Eubie Blake, qui inaugura le premier Vitaphone, ou film sonore : très simple, le son était assuré par un disque, synchronisé avec le film. On voit en effet E. BLAKE, jouant, ainsi enregistré, du piano, en 1922. Un "cake-walk" (danse à la mode) vers 1900. Louis ARMSTRONG chante, vers 1930, puis joue de la trompette (en orchestre)

le musicien Bud FREEMAN évoque l'importance d'ARMSTRONG. Et un document intéressant : en concert avec orchestre (probablement vers 1950), Louis ARMSTRONG et le tromboniste que fut Jack TEAGARDEN : un duo-gag intitulé "Rocking-chair": après une courte introduction trompette et trombone, les deux compères dialoguent en chantant avec réparties, et la voix d'ARMSTRONG. Un concours de danse dans les années 30 : des couples noirs dans des danses ultra-rapides et rythmées, dans un bistro. La chanteuse Mamie SMITH fait un duo humoristique, ressemblant à une scène de ménage, avec un pianiste-chanteur. La chanteuse de blues Bessie SMITH chante (assez court)

Brownie McGhee chante avec orchestre et choeurs (extrait d'un film). Une séance d'enregistrement de l' "Original Dixieland JASS Band" (style Nouvelle-Orléans). Evocation du trompettiste Bix BEIDERBECKE, "un blanc qui comprenait la musique noire mieux que personne". James Bubber MILEY, à la trompette, et Duke ELLINGTON, au piano : improvisation en duo (années 1930). L'orchestre de Duke ELLINGTON, au huppé et légendaire cabaret "Cotton Club" à New-York, donne une prestation avec danseurs.

title.title: Chaka Khan at the BBC
title.CE_synopsis:
Ain’t Nobody quite like Chaka Khan, and the proof of that comes courtesy of the BBC’s music archives, which have been plundered for this celebration of one of the all-time great queens of soul.
This selection of Chaka’s finest BBC moments covers five decades of performing, reflecting a career that started in the 70s with her partnership with Rufus and eventually led to the massive number one hit I Feel for You, which helped bring rap right into the mainstream, and I’m Every Woman, an instant anthem that made her a lifelong female icon.

title.title: De Wereld van Polygoon
CE_synopsis:
In Polygoonjournaals werd aandacht geschonken aan onderwerpen
als landbouw, het Koninklijk Huis en buitenlands nieuws. De
journaals circuleerden vaak wekenlang langs de Nederlandse
bioscopen. Polygoon gebruikte vrijwel direct in de jaren '20
geluidsfilms.

censuur door) de RVD en de ondergang van Polygoon door de
concurrentie van de televisie.

title.id: dim dam dom | spécial collections : printemps 1969 [1969-03-01]
title.title: Dim Dam Dom | Spécial collections : printemps 1969
title.CE_synopsis:
En plateau, Juliette de BOISRIVEAUD anime cette émission spéciale mode consacrée aux collections de printemps. Les mannequins présentent les modèles en évoluant au son de la musique jouée par les musiciens présents sur le plateau (musique pop et jazz). Les couturiers font de brèves déclarations quand leurs modèles défilent, souvent couverts par le son de la musqiue.
- Après une chorégraphie sur le générique, une présentation de modèles sur le thème de la transparence, présentation de modèles Nina Ricci. Gérard PIPART (pour Nina Ricci) s'exprime sur l'importance de la haute-couture. Sa voix est couverte par l'orchestre qui joue sur le plateau.
- Présentation de modèles Jean Patou en musique et coupé par une chorégraphie de danseuses de René Goliard. Michel GOMA (pour Jean Patou) dit quelques mots au sujet de sa collection, également couvert par la musique.
- Modèles Philippe VENET au son de l'orchestre avec chanteur et intervention du couturier.
- Prestation artistique du groupe The Web, suivie par Stan Getz et sa formation sur la présentation de mode Lanvin. Jules-François CRAHAY trouve que sa collection n'est pas si "audacieuse".
- Présentation de mode de jupes plissées au son d'une chanson.
- Des mannequins en perruques courtes de couleur et en tenues courtes de Courrèges, dansent au son d'une musique pop-rock. Au micro de Juliette de Boisriveaud, deux d'entre elles déclarent qu'elles porteraient ces modèles dans la rue.
- Présentation de robes longues Yves Saint-Laurent, sur le thème du patchwork, accompagnée par Ivan Rebroff qui chante un chant traditionnel en russe. La présentation continue avec les mannequins qui dansent sur la musique de Davy Jones et d'Ivan Rebroff en alternance.
- Chanson de Normando Marques dos Santos sur une présentation de robes en mousseline Yves Saint-Laurent et Pierre Cardin.
- Présentation de mode Ungaro sur une prestation artistique de Serge Gainsbourg et Jane Birkin, et sur une bande son musicale. Emanuel UNGARO déclare que "c'est la femme contemporaine qui l'intéresse".
- Des mannequins dansent sur le groupe The Nice qui joue sur le plateau. Elles portent des ensembles jupes et vestes houppelandes.
- Des mannequins portant des tenues Pierre Cardin dansent au son de la chanson de Neil Mc Arthur. Pierre CARDIN énumère des chiffres en cascades : "280 robes" dans sa collection, ... Dans "156 usines, dans 28 pays". Il déclare que Paris est "le tremplin de la mode pour le monde entier".
- Chanson de Françoise Hardy sur une présentation de modèles Christian Dior.
- Présentation de robes Paco Rabanne avec la prestation artistique de Wallis qui porte une robe en plaquettes de plastique et gros plans sur les détails de robes en métal et plastique. Paco RABANNE parle de la praticité de ses robes.
title.CE_tracklist:
- Le groupe LA QUESTION joue plusieurs morceaux en direct, sur des présentations de mode, sur le plateau.
- Le groupe THE WEB joue et chante en direct sur le plateau, d'abord un morceau instrumentale et ensuite "Baby won't you leave me alone", sur une présentation de mode tuniques et pantalons.
- Stan GETZ au saxophone, interprète deux sambas en direct sur le plateau, accompagné par Jack DEJOHNETTE à la batterie, Stanley COWELL au piano et Miroslav VITOUS à la basse, pendant la présentation de mode Lanvin.
- Ivan REBROFF chante (en play-back) un chant traditionnel russe, "Les Yeux noirs", à côté de mannequins portant des robes longues Yves Saint-Laurent.
- Davy JONES accompagné par le Voodoo Funk Machine chante (apparemment en direct) un extrait de "Mojo", coupé par Ivan REBROFF interprétant (play-back) en russe, un extrait de "Les Nuits de Moscou", sur une présentation de mode Yves Saint-Laurent.
- Normando MARQUES chante (apparemment en direct) un extrait de "Balanço com bossa" en s'accompagnant à la guitare et sur présentation de mode.
- Chorégraphie au son d'une musique d'inspiration indienne.
- Serge GAINSBOURG chante en play-back le début de "Elisa" tandis que Jane BIRKIN (dans une robe Ungaro ?) l'accompagne maladroitement à la batterie. En alternance, une présentation de mode Ungaro.
- Serge GAINSBOURG et Jane BIRKIN chantent en duo et en direct sur le plateau de l'émission, un extrait de la chanson "Ne dis rien".
- Françoise HARDY chante en play-back un extrait de "Comment te dire adieu". Elle porte un ensemble pantalon Christian Dior.
- Le groupe THE NICE joue en direct sur le plateau pendant que des mannequins dansent.
- Neil MC ARTHUR chante en play-back "She's not there" sur une présentation de mode Cardin.
- Françoise HARDY (toujours en ensemble Dior) chante en play-back, un extrait de "Etonnez-moi Benoît" sur une présentation de mode Christian Dior.
- Chorégraphie sur un thème de "Singing in the rain".
- WALLIS chante (en play-back) un extrait de "Johan", vêtue d'une robe Paco Rabanne en plaquettes de plastique.
- Le groupe THE NICE joue en direct "Rondo", sur une présentation de mode Paco Rabanne et sur le générique de fin.

title.title: Echoes of a Genius : Miles Davis in Europe
title.CE_synopsis: In search of Miles Davis's legacy and influence outside America, Ulli Pfau traces the most important steps of his European career and visits the places where Miles has left his European footprints. Speakers are musicians who worked with him (Dave Holland, John McLaughlin, Niels-Henning Ørsted Pedersen), festival directors (Claude Nobs, Montreux Jazz and Paul Acket, North Sea Jazz Festival) as well as Juliette Greco and Louis Malle who Miles met during the recordings of the legendary soundtrack for the film noir classic L'Ascenseur pour l'échafaud. In some rare archival interviews, Miles speaks of his European impressions and musical influences.

title.title: Europe Jazz
title.CE_synopsis: Une soirée dans un club de jazz à Bruxelles. Le film, avec un commentaire en anglais, commence par une présentation de Bruxelles, vue par un Américain. On voit successivement l'Hôtel de ville, la Grand-place, la rue Neuve, des trams, une galerie couverte, les grands boulevards, le Palais des Académies, le Palais-royal, le Sablon, un marché, le Marché aux puces, une marchande d'escargots, une friterie, un marchand de gaufres, le Cinéma Eldorado et la Place de Brouckère avec ses enseignes lumineuses, une série d'enseignes pour des bars et spectacles ("Lido", "La diligence", "Moulin rouge", "Chez Paul au Gaity", "La Guyane", "Le Boeuf sur le Toit", "Charly's", le "Black and White", "Show Boat") et enfin la Tour Martini. Nous sommes ensuite dans un bar, où se produit la formation suivante : Sadi (vibraphone), Toots Thielemans (harmonica et guitare), Benoît Quersin (basse), Robert Permet (batterie), Pierre Franzino (piano), Jacques Pelzer (saxophone), qui exécute plusieurs morceaux. De nombreux plans de coupe montrent le public, assis devant des bougies, fumant, buvant, s'embrassant. On y reconnaît : Wilhelmine, Françoise Levie, Paul Sterckx, Corneille Hannoset. Un couple quitte ensuite le bar, que l'on voit alors situé dans la Galerie du Roi, passe dans la Petite Rue des Bouchers et monte dans une voiture de sport décapotable.

title.CE_synopsis:

Interview de Jacques BENOIT-LEVY, un des organisateurs du Festival d'Antibes, qui parle du prochain Festival . Il rend hommage à l'ORTF et à la Municipalité d'Antibes-Juan les Pins.
Parade du 10 Juillet 1960 pour l'inauguration de la statue de Sidney BECHET : défilé de ses admirateurs, de musiciens, etc. dans les rues d'Antibes.

5ème festival de jazz d'Antibes - Juan les Pins
- Longue introduction avec de nombreux plans d'Antibes, la baie, croiseur américain, le port, des bateaux, baigneurs sur plage, enfants faisant des chateaux de sable, piétons dans les rues, cafés, les pins, guichet de location pour le festival, chaises vides, projecteurs allumés

 Après le générique : plan de ski nautique nocturne avec feu d'artifice sur l'eau.

title.id: festival de jazz d'antibes 1980 : the legends of jazz [1981-03-29]
title.title: Festival de jazz d'Antibes 1980 : The Legends of jazz
title.CE_synopsis: Spectacle "1000 YEARS OF JAZZ" donné au festival de jazz d'Antibes Juan-les-Pins le 25 juillet 1980 par THE LEGENDS OF JAZZ. A l'orchestre se joignent parfois la chanteuse Carol CASS et un quatuor de danseurs de claquettes THE ORIGINAL HOOFERS.
title.CE_tracklist:
Les différents musiciens regroupés en une formation baptisée "The LEGENDS OF JAZZ" (ou "1000 YEARS OF JAZZ") interprètent "Mama don't allow it " et "Caldonia". 
Ils accompagnent Carol CASS qui, enveloppée dans un spectaculaire boa rouge, chante" Basin street blues" et "Bill Bailey won't you please come home". Numéros de claquettes par the ORIGINAL HOOFERS, d'abord Ian CHANEY, puis Ralph BROWN (canotier, canne, magnifiques chaussures roses), Raymond KAALUND et Jimmy SLIDE.
THE LEGENDS OF JAZZ interprètent "I got rhythm", accompagnés de la chanteuse Carol CASS (avec une nouvelle tenue) et des quatre danseurs de claquettes THE ORIGINAL HOOFERS puis "Panama" et "Do you know what it means to miss New-Orleans?".
Carol CASS chante "Stormy weather", accompagnée de l'orchestre. 
THE LEGENDS OF JAZZ avec Sam LEE (chant et saxo) interprètent "Boogie Woogie". Sam LEE descend dans le public. 
Numéro de claquettes par THE ORIGINAL HOOFERS, ensemble puis solos de Ralph BROWN, Ian CHANEY et Jimmy SLIDE. 
THE LEGENDS OF JAZZ avec Carol CASS (dans une nouvelle tenue) interprètent "The joint is jumping". Elle est rejointe par THE ORIGINAL HOOFERS. Ils terminent par "When the saints go marchin in" et défilent (sur le générique) avec parapluies comme au Carnaval de la Nouvelle Orléans.

title.CE_synopsis: Retransmission en direct du festival de Chateauvallon 1972 (concert du 23 août 1972). André FRANCIS donne en off des précisions sur l'orchestre CTI SUMMER JAZZ que nous entendons pendant l'émission : CTI est le "label" du producteur Creed TAYLOR qui, à la différence des jam sessions organisées par Norman Granz, écrit des arrangements - modernes mais pas d'avant-garde - pour les principaux musiciens de jazz qu'il a sous contrat. Pour ce set, les musiciens réunis sur scène sont : les solistes Hank CRAWFORD (saxophone alto), Stanley TURRENTINE (saxophone ténor), Freddie HUBBARD (trompette), Airto MOREIRA ( percussions) accompagnés par Hubert LAWS ( flûte), Ron CARTER (basse), Bob JAMES (piano) et Jack DEJOHNETTE (batterie).

 - "Blues en sol" : solo (accompagné par piano, basse, batterie) de Hank CRAWFORD

 - "Red Clay" : solo (idem) de Freddie HUBBARD
 - Improvisation du percussionniste Airto MOREIRA.
 - courte jam session par tous les musiciens SUR LE GENERIQUE DE FIN. 
 
 NOTE: ces 5 morceaux ont été composés chacun par le soliste correspondant.

title.CE_synopsis:
Retransmission en direct du dernier concert du Festival de Chateauvallon 1971.
 André FRANCIS, à l'image sur la scène puis off annonce que ce Festival a rencontré un succès supérieur à ce qu'attendaient les organisateurs et "qu'il devrait en principe à nouveau avoir lieu l'année prochaine".
 - Nous écoutons le quartet du saxophoniste ténor Johnny GRIFFIN entouré de Vince BENEDETTI au piano, Alby CULLAZ à la basse, Art TAYLOR à la batterie. Au fil du concert, Johnny GRIFFIN est rejoint la guest star du soir, le trompettiste Dizzy GILLESPIE, puis ensuite par Stan GETZ. 
 - La partie concert diffusée s'interrompt après moins d'une heure, l'enregistrement du concert par contre couvre un peu moins d'une heure trente de leur prestation.

Le quartet de Johnny GRIFFIN interprète un premier morceau intitulé "Soft and funny".

- La première partie du concert précédent la partie diffusée figure dans le magnéto MGCPF0097232.01 (prestation du quartet Johnny GRIFFIN et Dizzy GILLEPSIE) et la partie du concert succédant à l'interruption de la diffusion figure dans le magnéto MGCPF0097232.02. Dans cette dernière partie, Stan GETZ joue avec Johnny GRIFFIN et Dizzy GILLEPSIE et sont rejoint par Virginia VEE (cette séquence a été diffusé ultérieurement dans le spécial Chateauvallon du 22/07/1972.

title.id: festival de jazz de chateauvallon : l'organic music theater de don cherry [1972-08-27]
title.title: Festival de jazz de Chateauvallon : L'Organic Music Theater de Don Cherry
title.CE_synopsis:
André FRANCIS annonce en off le programme de la soirée en direct du festival jazz de Chateauvallon : une musique "sortant des normes du jazz", l'ORGANIC MUSIC THEATER de Don CHERRY (un des précursseurs du free jazz avec Ornette Coleman). Aussi présenté sous le nom du "Don cherry New Researches", il s'agit d'une réunion de musiciens, ou plutôt d'une famille au sens strict et au sens large composé de danseurs, chanteurs et même d'enfants que don Cherry emmène communier sur "des sons et des mélodies de la planète Terre en 1972". Tout ce petit monde disposé en cercle sur la scène devant le public du festival est vêtu d'habits bariolés, se déplace au fur et à mesure du concert, jouant à l'occasion d'instruments de musique folkloriques ou animant des marionnettes géantes, dans un style très "Flower power". 
Le commentaire d'André FRANCIS explique: "Une musique naturelle, sans pudeur, simple, exprimant la joie intérieure, à la portée du plus grand nombre, ouverte à la communication, nourrie d'emprunts à la musique africaine et à celle de l'Inde".
title.CE_tracklist: Aucune indication de titre pour cette prestation de Don CHERRY, il s'agit d'une longue improvisation tout au long de l'émission.

title.CE_synopsis: I dag: Repriseflimre med Keith Jarrett, Jan Garbarek, Palle Danielsson og Jon Christensen. I opptaket i studio hører vi låtene "The Windup", "Long As You Know You're Living Yours", "Mandala" og "Blossom" Norsk musikkprogram (s-hv), opprinnelig sendt som programserien "Jazz" 6. og 13. mai 1974

title.title: Flimra | Musikkflimre med Gary Burton (1:2)
title.CE_synopsis: I dag: Musikkflimre med Gary Burton. (1:2) Fra en konsert på Club 7 i Oslo 25. november 1976. Flimra var tilstede og sender her et utdrag fra konserten. Gary Burton har tidligere opptrådt i norsk fjernsyn og holdt konserter på Club 7 og i Molde. Et nytt bekjentskap vil kanskje Dan Gottlieb, trommer, være. Han er forholdsvis fersk i gruppen, som foruten ham består av Gary Burton, vibrafon, Pat Metheny, elektrisk gitar, og Steve Swallow, elektrisk bass-gitar. I kveld spiller de "Open Your Eyes You Can Fly", "Vox Humana", "Falling Grace" og "Como en Vietnam". Norsk musikkprogram (s-hv). Billedregi: Svein Erik Børja.

title.title: Flimra | Musikkflimre med Gary Burton (2:2)
title.CE_synopsis: I dag: Musikkflimre med Gary Burton. (2:2) Fra en konsert på Club 7 i Oslo 25. november 1976. Flimra var tilstede og sender her annen del fra konserten. Gary Burton regnes som en toppgruppe innen jazzkretser, og består av fire musikere: Gary Burton, vibrafon, Pat Metheny, elektrisk gitar, Steve Swallow, elektrisk bass-gitar, og Dan Gottlieb, trommer. Konserten åpner med "Yellow Fields" av Eberhard Weber. Deretter følger tre melodier av Carla Bley: "Ictus", "Syndrome" og "Dreams So Real". Så kommer "Sea Journey" av Chick Corea og til slutt en låt av Pat Metheny, "Sirabforn". Norsk musikkprogram (s-hv). Billedregi: Svein Erik Børja.

Programma over dans op jazzmuziek.
Het Donald Byrd Combo improviseert op enkele klassieke jazzthema's.
Uitvoering van de "Fontessa Suite", een klassieke dans op jazz-muziek van John Lewis, uitgevoerd door het Modern Jazz Quartet en gedanst door het Ballet des Etoiles de Paris.
Rolverdeling: Fontessa - Yvonne Meyer

Pierrot - Ivan Dracadze.
Choreografie - Milko Sparemblek en Vasili Sulic.
Uitvoering van "Monotony" en "This is my theme", twee zogenaamde "mechanische dansen" waarbij poppetjes allerlei bewegingen uitvoeren, van Harry Kramer op jazzmuziek van Stan Kenton. Mmv zangeres June Christy.

title.title: Forum Musiques
title.CE_synopsis:
Dernière émission de la série de Jean Emile JEANNESSON et Michel PERICARD, qui propose en premier lieu une rediffusion du 23 octobre 1968 : les MOTHERS OF INVENTION dans un long extrait de musique instrumentale.
 Par ailleurs François BAYLE présente un exemple de musique concrète avec une séance de musique en studio en compagnie du groupe FREE FRENCH FORM TRIO ACTING . François BAYLE échange quelques reflexions avec les trois musiciens sur leur conception du son musical.
title.CE_tracklist:
TAJ MAHAL , chanteur noir américain chante le blues
FREE FRENCH FORM TRIO ACTING interprète en studio un extrait de leur composition 
 BRIGITTE LEFEVRE, NORBERT SCHMUCKI et JACQUES GARNIER de l'opéra, dansent en extérieur, sur la terrase du Palais de Chaillot, et sur la musique concrète du trio .

title.title: Forum Musiques | SPECIAL LONDRES
title.CE_synopsis:
- Interview par ANDRE MAURICE d'une jeune journaliste, KATE PAVIOT (au marché aux Puces "hippy" de Portobello), sur la place de la Pop Music dans la vie des jeunes
- Groupe Sam GOPAL "Bateau sur la Tamise" (première apparition à la tv française de Lemmy Kilmister, futur chanteur et bassiste du groupe Motorhead)
- Interview de quatre jeunes Anglais (deux garçons, deux filles) du lycée français de Londres sur la musique pop, les courants de musique et les rapports avec les parents à travers les goûts musicaux. Ils parlent aussi de la drogue, plutôt anti. Ils parlent aussi de la comédie musicale "Hair", de la nudité.
- LES SPOOKY TOOTH répétant dans la grange de leur cottage (improvisation sur le titre "Better By You, Better Than Me")
- THE JETHRO TULL au Morgan Studio pendant l'enregistrement de Pop Music
- Interview de TIM CURY, interprète de "Hair" de Londres. La pièce parle de liberté, d'amour le scénario perme d'improviser.
- PETER STRACKER, vedette de la version londonienne de "Hair", chante "Aquarius" et "Let the sun shine in", les deux airs principaux de "Hair" dans un studio.
- THE SOFT MACHINE : au Ronnie Scott's Club, nouvelle version de ce groupe en trio, orgue, basse, batterie.

title.CE_synopsis: Première émission de la collection proposée par Pierre André BOUTANG consacrée à la musique sous toutes ses formes. Après sa prestation, Michel POLNAREFF parle de son goût pour toutes les expressions musicales, puis de doctes présentateurs annoncent les différents artistes avec un discours très professoral.
title.CE_tracklist:
Accompagné par un orchestre, Michel POLNAREFF (tantôt au piano, tantôt au clavecin) interprète une suite anglaise de Bach (en partie sur générique début), puis un pot pourri de ses succès parmi lesquels "Ame câline" (instrumental uniquement), "La poupée qui fait non", "Jour après jour", "Love me, please love me". Puis il chante "Mes regrets" (dans son intégralité).
Les MOTHERS OF INVENTION , groupe américain de Pop-Music avec FRANK ZAPPA (pour la première fois en France) dirigeant le groupe, qui interprète une prestation, uniquement instrumentale , 10 minutes extraites d'une suite de 45 minutes.
MARIE NOELLE (16ans) accompagnée par MICHEL POLNAREFF (à la guitare) chante une chanson de sa composition "C'est comme"
Séquence de jazz avec PHIL WOOD - ballets sur ces airs de jazz de grande formation
Démonstration de karaté en attendant la grande première de Joe Cocker, l' un des meilleurs chanteurs anglais à l'heure actuelle, qui reprend une chanson des Beatles "With a little help from my friends" , puis qui chante une de ses compositions "Something's coming on" .

title.id: frank zappa : the present-day composer refuses to die [2000-07-02]
title.title: Frank Zappa : The Present-Day Composer Refuses To Die
CE_synopsis:
Adhv archiefmateriaal en interviews wordt een portret
geschilderd van het veelzijdige muzikale talent van
componist/gitarist Frank Zappa. Centraal staat daarbij de
wisselwerking tussen Zappa's band The Mothers of Invention en
Zappa. Aan de orde komen daarbij Zappa's stijl van componeren
en combineren, zijn desinteresse in klassieke muziek, het
Zappa-archief, de "Freak out"-opnames, Zappa's experimenten
met publiek in het Garrick Theatre, zijn gebruik van visuele
middelen, muzikale experimenten, de bestorming van het podium
tijdens een concert in Berlijn, Zappa's leiderschap bij de
band, het groeien van de band tijdens live-optredens,
tweesporen-opnames, de invloed van Zappa op zijn bandleden,
de regelmatige ontslagen die vielen onder de bandleden, het
instinctieve bespelen van instrumenten,
Zappa's unieke muziekstijl, het gebruik van het synclavier
door Zappa, zijn ziekte, het Varèse-project met het Ensemble
Contemporain in 1992 en het Amnerika-project.
INTERVIEWS hierover met:
- Gail Zappa, echtgenote van Zappa
- Tom Fowler, bandlid van The Mothers of Invention
- Ian Underwood, bandlid van The Mothers of Invention
- George Duke, bandlid van The Mothers of Invention

- Ali Naskin, musicus.

title.title: Gary Burtons Kvartett på Chat Noir
title.CE_synopsis: Norsk musikkprogram (s-hv). Jazzkonsert med Gary Burton Kvartett på Chat Noir i Oslo. Vibrafonisten Gary Burton regnes av mange som den største fornyer på sitt instrument siden Milt Jackson, og bare Bobby Hutcherson har i dag muligheten for å gjøre ham rangen stridig. Burtons kvartett er dessuten et av de sterkest sammensveisede ensembler i dagens jazz, og det er særlig samarbeidet mellom Burton og bassisten Steve Swallow som er gruppens drivkraft. Gary Burton Quartet består av Gary Burton, vibrafon. Steve Swallow, bass. David Pritchard, gitar. Bill Goodwin, trommer. Regi: Svein Erik Børja.

title.title: Gevoelige Snaren
CE_synopsis:
Muziekspecial over het Rosenberg Trio tgv hun tienjarig jubileum.
De leden van het Rosenberg Trio worden gevolgd tijdens hun dagelijks leven. Ze wonen op een woonwagenkamp nabij Nuenen en behoren tot de Sinti-zigeuners. Sinds tien jaar vormen ze met internationaal succes een muzikaal trio dat een mix vangipsy jazz en zigeunermuziek speelt. Er wordt met ze gesproken over hun zigeunerleven, hun muzikale opvoeding, de samenwerking met violist Jaap van Zweden, het niet kunnen lezen van bladmuziek, de loopbaan van het Rosenberg Trio, het familieleven, de invloed van de gipsy swing van Django Reinhardt en Stéphane Grapelli, de verschillende soorten muziek die ze in hun eigen muziek verwerken, de verschillen tussen de jazz van het Rosenberg Trio en zigeunermuziek, de masterclasses van Stochelo Rosenberg en hun koninklijke onderscheiding.

MGCPC0112846--AM.1 :
- Concert de Buddy GUY et Junior WELLS avec Buddy GUY à la guitare et Junior WELLS à l'harmonica et au chant, Phil GUY à la basse, Roosevelt SHAW à la batterie et James BOOKER au piano et au chant. La première partie du concert a pour leader James BOOKER qui chante et joue essentiellement seul. Buddy GUY et Junior WELLS n'apparaissent que dans un second temps lorsque James BOOKER se retire.
- Extrait du concert (manque la fin) de Gerry WIGGINS au piano, George DUVIVIER à la contrebasse, Oliver JACKSON à la batterie, Illinois JACQUET au saxophone ténor, David 'Fathead' NEWMAN au saxophone ténor et à la flûte et Hank CRAWFORD au saxophone alto, enregistré le 8 juillet 1978. MGCPC0112846--AM.3 :

CE_synopsis: Concert historique JATP - Jazz at the Philharmonic enregistré en novembre 1960 à la Salle Pleyel. Il s'agit d'une véritable jam session

en effet se suivent sur scène :
 - le tromboniste Jay Jay JOHNSON accompagné par un pianiste, un bassiste et un batteur (non identifiés), ce sont ceux-là même qui composent la section rythmique du quintet de Cannonball Adderley, quintet qui viendra sur scène dans une dizaine de minutes
J J JOHNSON interprète un thème
- le saxophoniste tenor Stan GETZ, accompagné par le même trio, qui joue un thème
- le quintet du saxophoniste alto Cannonball ADDERLEY, comprenant son frère Nat ADDERLEY et la même section rythmique

title.title: JATP Pleyel 1960 - 2ème partie
title.concert:
1960-11-25|Paris|Jazz at the Philharmonic - Dizzy Gillespie
1960-11-25|Paris|Jazz at the Philharmonic - Roy Eldridge/Benny Carter/Don Byas/Coleman Hawkins
CE_synopsis:
1ERE PARTIE.
Jam session comprenant Roy ELDRIDGE, Don BYAS, Coleman HAWKINS, Benny CARTER, Lalo SHIFRIN, Sam JONES et Jo JONES. Ils interprètent
 - "Indiana" en prenant chacun un solo, notamment solo virtuose de batterie de Jo JONES.

2EME PARTIE.
"Gillespiana", longue suite de thèmes composée par Lalo Shifrin et Dizzy Gillespie, qui marquait le début de l'intérêt de ce dernier pour les rythmes afro-cubains. Elle est interprétée par Dizzy GILLESPIE et les autres membres de son quintet.
Pour le dernier thème de "Gillespiana", un spécialiste cubain des percussions afro-cubaines s'adjoint au quintet: Candido CAMERO
il interprète un long solo très virtuose de bongo (gros tambour utilisé en musique latino-américaine, sur lequel on frappe avec les doigts) - solo en permanence accompagné par le batteur.
